ml.originalTitle: Vero: Can AI Agents Build Formally Verified Software Repositories?
ml.catchyTitle: Vero: Can AI Agents Build Formally Verified Software Repositories?
ml.summary: Vero is introduced, the first benchmark to evaluate joint implementation and proof synthesis at the repository level and an audit mechanism where agents are allowed to formally prove unsatisfiability of provided specification or incorrectness of reference code, which surfaces and corrects latent code and specification errors during curation.

ml.originalTitle: DARTree: Speculative Diffusion Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Trees
ml.catchyTitle: DARTree: Speculative Diffusion Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Trees
ml.summary: Speculative decoding losslessly accelerates autoregressive language models by verifying multiple draft tokens in parallel. Existing recurrent correction incorporates causal information along a single draft chain, whereas diffusion-based tree construction broadens candidate coverage without carrying this correction along individual branches. We introduce DARTree, a training-free speculative decoding method that extends a pretrained AR correction head from chains to trees.

ml.originalTitle: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically Controlled Knowledge Exposure
ml.catchyTitle: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically Controlled Knowledge Exposure
ml.summary: Modern language models are trained on heterogeneous web-scale text corpora. Consequently, studying knowledge and skill acquisition is difficult, as prior exposure to related content is hard to characterize. Training a 5B-parameter LLM from scratch on LITTLECURRICULUM yields LITTLELEARNER, a model with sufficient language competence for open-ended evaluation, yet with clear knowledge and capability boundaries mapped to interpretable curriculum guidelines.

ml.originalTitle: Exponential Convex Calibration Dimension for the Multi-Label Jaccard Measure
ml.catchyTitle: Exponential Convex Calibration Dimension for the Multi-Label Jaccard Measure
ml.summary: The per-instance Jaccard score, or intersection over union (IoU), is standard in multi-label classification and binary segmentation. Under the convention, we prove that the Jaccard score, shifted-loss, and ordinary loss matrices are nonsingular and that the loss columns have affine dimension. Thus zero-regret calibration requires exponential dimension, whereas every fixed additive regret tolerance admits polynomial prediction dimension.

ml.catchyTitle: Defensive Boosting for Online Probabilistic Forecasting
ml.summary: On every adaptive sequence, its Brier score is competitive with the best prediction induced by the span of at the same rate as online gradient boosting; simultaneously, whenever the realized transcript satisfies the smooth weak-learning condition, its Brier score and randomized classification error satisfy the same rate guarantee as online classification boosting.

ml.originalTitle: Construction of an Automated Quality Control Model for Industrial Waste Gas Online Monitoring Data Based on Unsupervised Learning
ml.catchyTitle: Construction of an Automated Quality Control Model for Industrial Waste Gas Online Monitoring Data Based on Unsupervised Learning
ml.summary: To address the limitations of conventional methods—namely, low recognition rates for sporadic equipment failures and emerging anomalous patterns, as well as a heavy reliance on manual labels—this paper constructs an automated quality control model for industrial waste gas online monitoring data based on unsupervised learning.

ml.originalTitle: SOAR: Smooth Online Activation Routing for Stable Neural Learning from Evolving Streams
ml.catchyTitle: SOAR: Smooth Online Activation Routing for Stable Neural Learning from Evolving Streams
ml.summary: Online neural learning requires models that update after each incoming example, remain calibrated under distributional change, and avoid brittle gradient transmission. This revision reformulates the problem as genuine prequential online learning and introduces Smooth Online Activation Routing (SOAR), a Hedge-style routing algorithm over smooth activation experts trained by singleinstance adaptive updates.

ml.catchyTitle: The construct of institutional distance through the lens of diverse institutional perspectives: Review, analysis, and future directions.
ml.summary: This paper presents a review and critique of the 20-year-old literature on institutional distance, which has greatly proliferated. We start with a discussion of the three institutional perspectives that have served as a theoretical foundation for this construct: organizational institutionalism, institutional economics, and comparative institutionalism. We conclude with actionable recommendations for improving institutional distance research.

nlp.catchyTitle: DFM Mimir v1: An Open HRM Delivering Frontier Performance at 1B Parameters Using Only Permissible Post-Training Data

nlp.originalTitle: SAEVerbalizer: Generating Explanations for Sparse Autoencoder Features via Representation Verbalization
nlp.catchyTitle: SAEVerbalizer: Generating Explanations for Sparse Autoencoder Features via Representation Verbalization
nlp.summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are proposed to extract numerous features from large language model (LLM) representations, yet explaining these features still relies primarily on external observation. We introduce SAEVerbalizer, a framework that injects SAE decoder directions into an LLM's representations and fine-tunes the LLM's downstream layers to generate natural-language explanations of the injected features.

nlp.catchyTitle: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically Controlled Knowledge Exposure

nlp.originalTitle: OmniScientist: An Omni-Modal Omni-Discipline AI Scientist
nlp.catchyTitle: OmniScientist: An Omni-Modal Omni-Discipline AI Scientist
nlp.summary: Recent advances in foundation models have enabled AI scientists to automate increasingly complete research workflows, from hypothesis generation and code execution to manuscript preparation. Yet workflow coverage alone does not provide access to the full evidence on which scientific discovery depends. We introduce OmniScientist, an end-to-end, omni-modal AI scientist that conducts multidisciplinary research directly from heterogeneous raw evidence.

nlp.originalTitle: AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design
nlp.catchyTitle: AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design
nlp.summary: In this paper, we present AutoDesign, a framework that aligns with human design priors, where a meta-harness optimizer guides a code agent to recursively improve harness based on rollout feedback. On the PosterBench Main Track, AutoDesign achieves the highest score of 78.32, surpassing the closed-source commercial system Claude Design by 7.45 points.

nlp.originalTitle: Response Format and Construct Validity in Medical Students' Word‑Analysis Assessment: A Validity Argument Approach
nlp.catchyTitle: Response Format and Construct Validity in Medical Students' Word‑Analysis Assessment: A Validity Argument Approach
nlp.summary: Response format may influence the interpretation of language assessment scores by engaging different cognitive processes. This study aimed to examine the effects of response format on medical students' word-analysis performance. A within-subjects counterbalanced comparative assessment design was employed with 170 undergraduate medical students who completed both a Multiple-Choice Word Analysis Test (MCQ) and a Word Analysis Completion Test (WACT).

nlp.originalTitle: Sentiment Analysis Performance of Lora-Enhanced Llm's
nlp.catchyTitle: Boosting Sentiment Analysis: How LoRA Supercharges DistilBERT on Social Media
nlp.summary: This study evaluates eight machine learning, deep learning, and transformer models for Twitter sentiment analysis. Fine-tuning DistilBERT with LoRA achieved the highest accuracy at 82.38%. The findings highlight that parameter-efficient fine-tuning significantly outperforms traditional approaches in short-text classification.

nlp.originalTitle: Comparing and Contrasting Forced Aligned Acoustic Models for Vernacular Speech
nlp.catchyTitle: Tuning in to Vernacular: Testing Forced Alignment on Appalachian English
nlp.summary: This study evaluated the Montreal Forced Aligner on Appalachian English using a pretrained model compared to manual alignment. With low error rates between 0.54% and 1.3%, the aligner handled dialect variations effectively. Researchers can reliably use this tool for vernacular speech analysis on high-quality recordings.

cv.originalTitle: Alaya-EVOKE: From Linear-Scaling Supervision to Endless World
cv.catchyTitle: Alaya-EVOKE: From Linear-Scaling Supervision to Endless World
cv.summary: Interactive world models must support persistent memory, responsive interaction, and long-horizon generation, yet these requirements place conflicting demands on the model. Maintaining history in the denoiser context or key-value cache incurs growing cost, forcing a trade-off between session length and retained memory, while low-latency interaction relies on few-step generation whose capabilities are bounded by its teacher.

cv.originalTitle: PlayWorld: Benchmarking World Models with Agent Players over Long-Horizon Objectives
cv.catchyTitle: PlayWorld: Benchmarking World Models with Agent Players over Long-Horizon Objectives
cv.summary: Video world models simulate future states conditioned on current observations and user actions. To address this, we employ multi-modal Agent Players to interact with world models toward specified long-horizon objectives. Experiments across nine state-of-the-art world models reveal that current models remain unreliable on long-horizon interactive objectives, particularly in maintaining spatial consistency and persistent state evolution.

cv.originalTitle: HumanTracker: Towards Comprehensive and Human-Aligned Motion Tracking Benchmark
cv.catchyTitle: HumanTracker: Towards Comprehensive and Human-Aligned Motion Tracking Benchmark
cv.summary: Humanoid motion tracking is central to teleoperation and whole-body imitation, yet evaluation often disagrees with what people perceive in videos. We introduce HumanTracker to make humanoid tracking evaluation both perceptually aligned and scalable. The HumanTracker benchmark contains approximately 153 hours of optical motion trajectories from multiple professional performers, organized into four motion families with text labels for fine-grained diagnosis.

cv.originalTitle: V-RAE: Rethinking Video Latent Spaces for Generation
cv.catchyTitle: V-RAE: Rethinking Video Latent Spaces for Generation
cv.summary: Latent video generation relies on autoencoders to define a compact space in which generative models operate. We propose V-RAE, a video representation autoencoder that builds compact generative latents on top of frozen vision foundation model representations. Beyond video generation, V-RAE also improves future video prediction on Cityscapes over the Wan 2.2 VAE latent space under matched prediction settings.

cv.catchyTitle: Stopping Exam Cheaters: Lightweight Real-Time Facial Recognition for Browser-Based Testing
cv.summary: This study introduces a browser-based facial recognition system to prevent student impersonation in computer-based exams. Built with face-api.js and liveness detection, it achieved 94.7% verification accuracy with fast response times. The scalable framework offers a secure biometric solution that upholds academic integrity.

cv.catchyTitle: Seeing Beyond Visible Light: How Multiband Imaging is Transforming Modern Agriculture
cv.summary: This review explores multiband imaging techniques that capture multiple spectral bands across the electromagnetic spectrum. By surpassing standard single-channel vision, this approach provides deeper analytical insights. Consequently, it plays a vital role in advancing precision agriculture to boost food production.

ai-health.originalTitle: MMHBench: A Multi-Perspective Benchmark for Mental Health Understanding in Long-Form Videos
ai-health.catchyTitle: MMHBench: A Multi-Perspective Benchmark for Mental Health Understanding in Long-Form Videos
ai-health.summary: Mental health understanding in long-form videos requires nuanced reasoning over observable behavior, interpersonal context, and latent psychological states. To address this limitation, we introduce MMHBench, a comprehensive multimodal benchmark for multi-perspective mental health understanding, comprising 268 long-form videos and 2,184 carefully curated questions.

ai-health.originalTitle: Anticipatory Digital Twins for Online Head-and-Neck Adaptive Proton Therapy via Foundation-Model Registration
ai-health.catchyTitle: Anticipatory Digital Twins for Online Head-and-Neck Adaptive Proton Therapy via Foundation-Model Registration
ai-health.summary: A first registration aligns a prior patient's planning CT to the target and carries the prior's during-treatment quality assurance CT (QACT) into the target frame; a second registration estimates the prior's planning-to-QACT change, which is then applied to the target's own planning CT to synthesize predicted CTs (pdCTs) with propagated contours.

ai-health.originalTitle: TumorBoard: Evidence-Grounded Multi-Agent Decision Support for Longitudinal Neuro-Oncology
ai-health.catchyTitle: TumorBoard: Evidence-Grounded Multi-Agent Decision Support for Longitudinal Neuro-Oncology
ai-health.summary: Neuro-oncology decisions require coordinated interpretation of serial MRI, pathology, molecular markers, treatment history, performance status, and evolving guidelines. We present TumorBoard, a multi-agent decision-support system built around a shared longitudinal case state and an auditable claim-evidence ledger. The safety governor reduced harmful release by 7.8 percentage points at a false-deferral cost of 4.3 percentage points.

Natural Language Processing (NLP) models predicting mental health outcomes rarely specify what they measure: contextual knowledge, emotional content, or syntactic structure. Sociodemographics alone explained no meaningful variance in depression, anxiety, or stress, but did so for life satisfaction, where emotion features and income were the strongest predictors; neuroticism and network topology instead dominated depression and anxiety, reversing direction between them.

ai-health.originalTitle: PatientAct: Theory-Grounded Mental Health Client Simulation
ai-health.catchyTitle: PatientAct: Theory-Grounded Mental Health Client Simulation
ai-health.summary: We present PatientAct, a framework for client simulation grounded in established clinical theories. If the therapist approaches gated content, PatientAct expresses resistance in terms of quantity, content, and style rather than defaulting to cooperation or a single resistance pattern. Moreover, PatientAct significantly outperforms the baselines, yielding substantial gains in resistance quality and behavioral realism.

llm.catchyTitle: MARC v1: An Open-Source Multi-Agent Framework for Clinical AI Reasoning and Coordination
llm.summary: We present Multi-Agent Reasoning and Coordination (MARC), an open-source framework that replaces monolithic LLM prompting with deterministic multi-agent orchestration for clinical reasoning. MARC coordinates role-specialized agents for extraction, reasoning, answer generation, and evaluation, with explicit context passing and traceable intermediate outputs, enabling stage-wise failure attribution. The full framework is available at https://github.com/Penn-RAIL/MARC-v1.

llm.originalTitle: Toward a Gricean Retreat: Probing LLMs for Knowledge Boundaries and Referent Specificity
llm.catchyTitle: Toward a Gricean Retreat: Probing LLMs for Knowledge Boundaries and Referent Specificity
llm.summary: We ask whether LLMs have the ingredients to perform this retreat. Using a T-REx-based benchmark that varies entity familiarity and referent specificity, we probe models to answer two questions: (i) do their activations encode whether a referent falls inside the knowledge boundary, and (ii) do they anticipate the specificity of the referent they are about to generate?

The purpose of this study is to evaluate the accuracy of the Montreal Forced Aligner (MFA) when analysing non-mainstream dialects. To achieve this, the alignment from a pretrained speech model was compared to hand aligned data. Altogether, there was 0.54–1.3% of errors that occurred across speakers.

llm.catchyTitle: Sentiment Analysis Performance of Lora-Enhanced Llm's
llm.summary: Sentiment analysis is mostly applied to short texts. In this study,experimental comparisons of large language models (LLMs), known deep learning and machinelearning algorithms are made using a dataset containing content from Twitter (X) users. It isanticipated that this study will be an important guide in applications such as sentiment analysis,where model selection is important.

robotics.originalTitle: Mind the Context: Continual Learning of Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via Environmental-Social Disentanglement
robotics.catchyTitle: Mind the Context: Continual Learning of Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via Environmental-Social Disentanglement
robotics.summary: Social robots are expected to operate across diverse environments, where similar arrangements can imply different socially appropriate actions, e.g., starting a conversation may be acceptable in a crowded home but disruptive in an office meeting. Experiments show that EDD outperforms several state-of-the-art baselines, and ablation studies further evaluate different disentanglement strategies and the sensitivity to domain ordering.

robotics.originalTitle: Decoding Task Progress from VLA Representations
robotics.catchyTitle: Decoding Task Progress from VLA Representations
robotics.summary: We use the probe as a simple label-free OOD detector, which detects stalled task progress, and find it competitive with state-of-the-art methods. Our results suggest that VLAs have rich, linearly readable internal representations of semantic quantities like task progress, and that learning to read these signals offers a lightweight, interpretable path toward monitoring deployed visuomotor policies.

robotics.originalTitle: DreamX-Phi 1.0: Action-Conditioned Video World Model for Robotic Manipulation
robotics.catchyTitle: DreamX-Phi 1.0: Action-Conditioned Video World Model for Robotic Manipulation
robotics.summary: We present DreamX-Phi 1.0, an action-conditioned video world model for robotic manipulation that, given an observed frame, a language instruction, and a prescribed action sequence comprising end-effector poses and gripper states, predicts the resulting future observations. Yet realism alone does not guarantee faithfulness: a convincing rollout can still move the wrong arm or lose the manipulated object.

robotics.originalTitle: A Browser-Native Digital Test Range for Benchmarking 4D Ocean-Glider Planning Algorithms
robotics.catchyTitle: A Browser-Native Digital Test Range for Benchmarking 4D Ocean-Glider Planning Algorithms
robotics.summary: Repeated in-situ evaluation of ocean-glider planners requires scarce vehicles, operators, deployment and recovery resources, and ocean conditions that cannot be reset for competing algorithms. We present a guided, installation-free browser-native digital test range that transforms a selected region into a reproducible four-dimensional experiment. Separately, source-locked GliderFlight 1.2.0 achieved native-to-browser parity through Pyodide/WebAssembly, establishing a pathway for high-fidelity multi-tier simulation.

robotics.catchyTitle: HumanTracker: Towards Comprehensive and Human-Aligned Motion Tracking Benchmark
robotics.summary: Humanoid motion tracking is central to teleoperation and whole-body imitation, yet evaluation often disagrees with what people perceive in videos. We introduce HumanTracker to make humanoid tracking evaluation both perceptually aligned and scalable. The HumanTracker benchmark contains approximately 153 hours of optical motion trajectories from multiple professional performers, organized into four motion families with text labels for fine-grained diagnosis.

cybersecurity.originalTitle: TopoIntent: Compiling Security Intent into Executable, Compliance-Checked Network Topologies
cybersecurity.catchyTitle: TopoIntent: Compiling Security Intent into Executable, Compliance-Checked Network Topologies
cybersecurity.summary: Enterprise security topology design requires translating business intent, regulatory requirements, and risk assumptions into zones, boundary devices, inter-zone paths, and access-control policies. Existing NetOps automation tools mainly operate after this design is fixed, providing limited support for generating structured security topologies from underspecified natural-language requirements. We present TopoIntent, a system that compiles security intent into executable, compliance-checked network topologies.

cybersecurity.originalTitle: TeleGapper: On the (un)reliability of Privacy Policies in Telegram Mini apps
cybersecurity.catchyTitle: TeleGapper: On the (un)reliability of Privacy Policies in Telegram Mini apps
cybersecurity.summary: Telegram Mini Apps are Web applications embedded within the Telegram client, forming an ecosystem of third-party services within one of the world's most widely used messaging platforms. Privacy disclosures are therefore critical for transparency. Telegram allows Mini Apps either to define an application-specific privacy policy or to rely on a platform-provided default policy.

cybersecurity.originalTitle: Does Fixing Break Security? An Empirical Study of Security Degradation in Iterative LLM-Driven Infrastructure-as-Code Repair
cybersecurity.catchyTitle: Does Fixing Break Security? An Empirical Study of Security Degradation in Iterative LLM-Driven Infrastructure-as-Code Repair
cybersecurity.summary: Background: Iterative feedback loops are the dominant paradigm for improving LLM-generated Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC): validators such as Checkov and terraform validate feed error signals back for successive repair attempts. Aims: We study security regression (a previously-passing CIS Benchmark check that fails after a repair iteration) to determine whether and how often iterative LLM repair degrades security while fixing other issues.

cybersecurity.originalTitle: LLM-Assisted Dynamic Threat Analysis for Attacker-Reachable Software Weaknesses in Autonomous Vehicles
cybersecurity.catchyTitle: LLM-Assisted Dynamic Threat Analysis for Attacker-Reachable Software Weaknesses in Autonomous Vehicles
cybersecurity.summary: Autonomous vehicles depend on large safety-critical software stacks, where weaknesses reachable from adversarial inputs may affect steering, braking, or other control decisions. No candidate weakness was dynamically confirmed within budget. These results show that build integration, not candidate generation or fuzzing, is the primary barrier to reliable LLM-assisted dynamic analysis of full autonomous-vehicle software stacks.

cybersecurity.originalTitle: Concept Drift Detection and Adaptive Retraining of Malware Classification Models
cybersecurity.catchyTitle: Concept Drift Detection and Adaptive Retraining of Malware Classification Models
cybersecurity.summary: For each of these models, we consider three distinct scenarios: A static scenario where no model retraining occurs, a periodic scenario where models are constantly retrained irrespective of concept drift, and a drift-aware scenario where models are only retrained when concept drift is detected. In addition, drift-aware retraining based on our OCSVM technique generally outperforms the MK-Means and MMD approaches.

cybersecurity.originalTitle: Antitrust Regulation of Algorithmic "Platform-Driven Involution'': From Governing the Corporate Person to Governing the Platform Ecosystem
cybersecurity.catchyTitle: Antitrust Regulation of Algorithmic "Platform-Driven Involution'': From Governing the Corporate Person to Governing the Platform Ecosystem
cybersecurity.summary: This article reconstructs ``platform-driven involution'' as a testable, portfolio-based theory-of-harm framework rather than a freestanding antitrust offense. The article clarifies that ecosystem analysis supplements rather than replaces relevant-market analysis and develops an evidence architecture for separating platform-induced effects from macroeconomic, demand, cost, and merchant-specific confounders.

data-science.originalTitle: Wasserstein Filtering: A Sample Selection Method for Robust Distribution Learning
data-science.catchyTitle: Wasserstein Filtering: A Sample Selection Method for Robust Distribution Learning
data-science.summary: This work proposes Wasserstein Filtering (WF), a novel sample selection framework that discards a fraction of suspicious samples and estimates the target distribution using the empirical measure of the remaining data, and proves that the WF estimator achieves minimax optimality over distribution families with bounded covariance.

data-science.originalTitle: Bagging Robustly Learns VC Classes with Linear Sample Complexity
data-science.catchyTitle: Bagging Robustly Learns VC Classes with Linear Sample Complexity
data-science.summary: We prove that VC classes are adversarially robustly learnable with sample complexity linear in the VC dimension, providing an exponential improvement over the previous upper bound of Montasser, Hanneke, and Srebro (2019). Remarkably, this result is achieved with a simple improper algorithm that combines the classic heuristic bagging (bootstrap aggregation) of Breiman (1996) with robust empirical risk minimization (RERM).

data-science.originalTitle: The data geometry of masking diffusion: Certified-optimal schedules via unmasking growth complexity
data-science.catchyTitle: The data geometry of masking diffusion: Certified-optimal schedules via unmasking growth complexity
data-science.summary: We study masking diffusion for discrete sampling and introduce a path-resolved measure of data geometry called the unmasking growth complexity ( UGC ). This leads to certified-optimal samplers that achieve a prescribed KL error with high probability and iteration complexity within a constant factor of the corresponding oracle procedure.

data-science.originalTitle: Exponential Convex Calibration Dimension for the Multi-Label Jaccard Measure
data-science.catchyTitle: Exponential Convex Calibration Dimension for the Multi-Label Jaccard Measure
data-science.summary: The per-instance Jaccard score, or intersection over union (IoU), is standard in multi-label classification and binary segmentation. Under the convention, we prove that the Jaccard score, shifted-loss, and ordinary loss matrices are nonsingular and that the loss columns have affine dimension. Thus zero-regret calibration requires exponential dimension, whereas every fixed additive regret tolerance admits polynomial prediction dimension.

data-science.originalTitle: Defensive Boosting for Online Probabilistic Forecasting
data-science.catchyTitle: Defensive Boosting for Online Probabilistic Forecasting
data-science.summary: On every adaptive sequence, its Brier score is competitive with the best prediction induced by the span of at the same rate as online gradient boosting; simultaneously, whenever the realized transcript satisfies the smooth weak-learning condition, its Brier score and randomized classification error satisfy the same rate guarantee as online classification boosting.

data-science.originalTitle: Fast Solution Methods for the Classical 0–1 Knapsack Problem
data-science.catchyTitle: Fast Solution Methods for the Classical 0–1 Knapsack Problem
data-science.summary: The classical 0--1 knapsack problem is among the simplest integer programs to state and among the most instructive problems for understanding why algorithm selection must follow instance structure. Small item counts favor meet-in-the-middle search, moderate capacities or total profits favor dynamic programming, favorable density structure favors core-based exact methods, and very large numeric coefficients favor approximation.

data-science.originalTitle: Measuring Activity-Space Segregation with Multi-Source Big Data: A Physical--Digital Framework with Simulation Validation and a Real-Data Proof of Concept
data-science.catchyTitle: Measuring Activity-Space Segregation with Multi-Source Big Data: A Physical--Digital Framework with Simulation Validation and a Real-Data Proof of Concept
data-science.summary: Segregation research increasingly measures who people encounter beyond home, yet physical mobility, place semantics, and digital activity are often combined without clear construct boundaries. This study develops a physical--digital activity-space framework that distinguishes co-presence, digital exposure, and digital interaction, and represents physical and digital segregation as separate components rather than a forced composite.

bio.originalTitle: SVPLEX: A Nextflow Pipeline for Cohort-level Structural Variant Calling
bio.catchyTitle: SVPLEX: A Nextflow Pipeline for Cohort-level Structural Variant Calling
bio.summary: SVPLEX is a Nextflow pipeline for cohort-level structural variant detection from short-read whole-genome sequencing data. The pipeline implements six different structural variant callers with different strengths and weaknesses, integrating different levels of evidence for SVs, and generates a merged consensus callset across the analysis cohort. SVPLEX is available on GitHub (bahlolab/SVPLEX) and is licensed under the MIT open-source licence.

bio.originalTitle: Task- and dataset-specific information in protein language models
bio.catchyTitle: Task- and dataset-specific information in protein language models
bio.summary: Protein language models (PLMs) have transferred the latest advances from natural language processing to computational biology. Embeddings from shallow layers of PLMs perform better for datasets that contain deep mutational scan (DMS) data, while datasets containing diverse natural proteins find most useful embeddings in the models' deeper layers.

bio.originalTitle: Static analysis-guided agentic AI translation enables Rust as a full stack bioinformatics language
bio.catchyTitle: Static analysis-guided agentic AI translation enables Rust as a full stack bioinformatics language
bio.summary: The field of bioinformatics struggles with legacy code - old code that is commonly used but may no longer have a maintainer, or may be written in an now-unfamiliar language (e.g. Perl, Fortran). Here we show that agentic AI, combined with static analysis, can be used to translate legacy code to the modern language Rust.

bio.originalTitle: Scan-Coil Delay Causes Anisotropic Signal Loss in Fast 4D-STEM
bio.catchyTitle: Scan-Coil Delay Causes Anisotropic Signal Loss in Fast 4D-STEM
bio.summary: Using direct probe imaging and sub-frame diffraction analysis, we document a significant intra-dwell scan-coil delay that systematically smears the recorded signal anisotropically along the fast scan direction, with a settling timescale of several tens of microseconds.

bio.originalTitle: Localize, Then Reason: Visual Latent Structural Reasoning for Molecular Properties and Edits
bio.catchyTitle: Localize, Then Reason: Visual Latent Structural Reasoning for Molecular Properties and Edits
bio.summary: Local chemical perception and property reasoning are both essential for understanding how molecular structure determines properties. Current LLM-based chemical reasoning methods either receive SMILES/molecular images together with descriptions of local motifs, or reason directly from molecular images. To address this gap, we propose Visual Latent Structural Reasoning (VLSR), an end-to-end framework that jointly learns localization and reasoning from molecular images.
